chapter.title: Angles and Shapes
chapter.tagline: Exploring turns, right angles, clock hands, and geometry in the physical body
chapter.overview: Through the fun 'Statue' game, students rotate their bodies and discover that angles measure amount of turning. They build cardboard angle testers to verify right angles (90°), explore acute and obtuse angles on clock faces, and find angles in everyday yoga postures.

sections.title: The Statue Game: Full, Half, and Quarter Turns
sections.subtitle: Experiencing angles as physical rotational turns

storyNarrative.dialogue: Rotate slowly... and STATUE! How far did you turn? A quarter turn faces you to your right; a half turn turns you all the way backward!

concept.heading: Angles as Rotational Amount
concept.keyRule: An angle measures the degree of turning between two intersecting lines or rays sharing a common vertex.

sections.title: The Angle Tester & The Right Angle
sections.subtitle: Building a simple L-shaped cardboard tester to detect 90° angles

storyNarrative.dialogue: Look at my two cardboard strips joined with a brass pin! When it forms an 'L' shape, it matches the corner of my book!

concept.heading: The Right Angle Standard
concept.keyRule: A right angle corresponds to a quarter turn (90°). Corners of books, doors, and window panes form right angles.

sections.title: Acute & Obtuse Angles on Clock Hands
sections.subtitle: Classifying angles smaller or greater than a right angle

storyNarrative.dialogue: At 3:00, the clock hands make a right angle! At 2:00, the angle is smaller (acute), and at 5:00, it opens wider (obtuse)!

concept.heading: Classification of Angles
concept.keyRule: Acute: less than 90° (< right angle). Right: exactly 90°. Obtuse: between 90° and 180° (> right angle).
